summary: On the main deck, Tank, Morpheus, and Trinity stare transfixed as the scrolling code accelerates 'faster and faster,' then blurs 'into streaks, shimmering ribbons of light that open like windows.' Each screen then fills with 'brilliant, saturated color images of Neo standing in the hall.' Tank can only stammer, 'How...?!' Morpheus answers with certainty, 'He is the one. He is the one!' Their realization is cut short when 'An EXPLOSION shakes the entire ship.'

what_changes.before: staring transfixed as the scrolling code accelerates, unable to interpret it
what_changes.after: seeing Neo on the screens, prompting Morpheus to declare him the one
what_changes.evidence: Each screen fills with brilliant, saturated color images of Neo standing in the hall.

what_changes.after: certain and exultant that Neo is the one
what_changes.evidence: He is the one.  He is the one!

what_changes.before: absorbed in awe at the monitors coming alive
what_changes.after: jolted by a violent explosion aboard the ship
what_changes.evidence: An EXPLOSION shakes the entire ship.

event_hint.one_line: The crew witnesses Neo's return on the screens just as the ship is attacked.

uncertain: Who or what caused the explosion.
Whether Trinity is among those who 'begin to blur into streaks' or only Tank and Morpheus.

minds.wants: To comprehend what the screens are showing before it resolves into something he can name.
minds.feels: Overwhelmed and cognitively outpaced — the code is accelerating beyond what his operator's mind can parse, and the arrival of live color images of a man he believed dead short-circuits his understanding entirely.
minds.shows: A single stammered 'How...?!' — the question of mechanism, not meaning. He asks how it is possible rather than declaring what it means.
minds.basis: Tank is described staring 'transfixed with awe' as code accelerates 'faster and faster, as if the machine language was unable to keep up or perhaps describe what is happening.' His only line is the fractured 'How...?!' This follows sc-215, where he was already at the monitors when they 'jump back to life,' and the whole crew has been operating under the belief that Neo was killed.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus has reached a certainty Tank himself cannot yet reach — that Morpheus understands what Tank does not.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus's certainty is not comprehension but faith; he is reading the event as prophecy fulfilled, not as a technical phenomenon he has decoded. Tank treats the declaration as an answer when it is really a different kind of knowing altogether.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is dead or lost — the 'How...?!' presupposes an impossibility.
believes_about.wrong_because: sc-216 shows Neo very much alive, having stopped the bullets and begun to see the Matrix as code. Tank's disbelief is already obsolete.

minds.wants: To affirm, aloud and finally, that what he has long believed has been confirmed — to have his faith validated in front of his crew at the moment of its apparent impossibility.
minds.feels: Exultant, vindicated. The repetition — 'He is the one. He is the one!' — is not explanation but a man steadying himself in the intensity of a conviction made real; the wonder he feels is religious, not analytical.
minds.shows: Certainty and near-triumph. Where Tank stammers a question of mechanics, Morpheus offers a declaration of identity. He lets the awe show but channels it entirely into conviction rather than confusion.
minds.basis: His line is a doubled, emphatic assertion of Neo's identity as 'the one,' delivered the instant the color images appear — the same 'miracle' the crew reacted to in sc-215 ('It is a miracle'). His reading of events as prophetic fulfillment is his established stance throughout the story.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is definitively 'the one' — the prophesied savior — and that these images are proof of it.
believes_about.wrong_because: The images prove only that Neo has returned and gained power none of them anticipated (sc-216 shows him stopping bullets and seeing the code). Whether that makes him the prophecy's figure is Morpheus's interpretation laid over the evidence, not something the evidence itself establishes.

believes_about.belief: That Tank's 'How...?!' is a question awaiting an answer Morpheus has already supplied.
believes_about.wrong_because: Tank is asking about mechanism — how a dead man is broadcasting live — and no declaration of identity actually addresses that. Morpheus hears his own certainty as the answer when it sidesteps the question entirely.

minds.wants: To hold onto the return of the man she loves and let the miracle land — she has already, in sc-215, been the one to voice the miracle and to command Neo back ('Now get up!').
minds.feels: A private, overwhelming relief and wonder that Neo is alive — the emotional stakes for her are personal, not prophetic, and this is the payoff of her desperation moments earlier.
minds.shows: Nothing audible here; she is grouped with the others 'staring transfixed with awe.' Her inner response is legible only through what she did in sc-215 (screaming when the monitors returned, urging Neo), so in this beat she lets the crew's reaction carry what she feels silently.
minds.basis: She is present among the three 'transfixed with awe,' and the uncertain field flags whether she is among those watching the code blur. sc-215 established her as the most emotionally invested — she screams at the monitors returning and commands Neo to rise — which frames her silence here as absorbed feeling rather than absence of it.

believes_about.belief: That Neo has somehow survived and returned to them.
believes_about.wrong_because: inferred — The evidence supports it (he is alive in sc-216), so this belief happens to be correct; what she cannot yet know is the nature of the change in him, that he now sees and commands the Matrix in ways that will reshape what he is to all of them.

connects_back: sc-215: the monitors 'jump back to life' and the crew's 'It is a miracle' — this scene is the payoff of that resurrection they could not yet explain.
sc-215: Trinity's 'Now get up!' and the crew's shared belief that Neo was lost, which makes the live images of him a genuine shock rather than an expected event.
sc-216: Neo stopping the bullets, seeing the code, and the bullet-reflection morph into the 'real' image — the source of the 'brilliant, saturated color images' now on the ship's screens.
The crew's long-standing investment in the prophecy of 'the one,' which is what allows Morpheus to read Neo's return as confirmation rather than anomaly.
sets_up: ev-035: The explosion that ends this scene initiates the hovercraft's fight for survival — Morpheus activating the EMP and Neo's final unplugging and reunion with Trinity.
The crew's now-solidified certainty that Neo is 'the one,' which underwrites Neo's authority to deliver the message to the Matrix in ev-036.
The momentum of Neo's transformed power, which carries directly into the lobby assault (ev-037) where that power is exercised openly.
dramatic_function: This scene converts a private miracle (Neo's resurrection in sc-216) into a public, witnessed confirmation for the crew — and specifically crystallizes Morpheus's faith into certainty — right before violently undercutting the triumph with the explosion, so that awe and imminent destruction collide and the story is knocked from revelation into survival.
